# atlc

**Computes impedance of a transmission line of any cross-section, from a picture of it**

- **Version recorded:** 4.6.1
- **Categories:** `antenna`, `electronics`
- **Upstream:** <https://tracker.debian.org/pkg/atlc>

## What it does

You draw the cross-section of a transmission line as a bitmap -- conductors in one colour, each dielectric in another -- and it solves the field numerically to give characteristic impedance, capacitance, inductance, velocity factor and loss. Coax, twin-lead, stripline, or a shape no formula covers: it does not care, because it is not using a formula.

## Why you would want it

Every closed-form impedance equation assumes a geometry. The moment you build something the textbook does not have -- a coax with an off-centre conductor, a balun wound on an odd former, an air-spaced line with supports, a stripline on a board with two dielectrics -- the equations stop applying and this is the tool that still answers. It is also how you check a homemade line before trusting it with power.

## Before it will work

A bitmap of the cross-section, drawn to a colour convention the manual specifies, and the patience to make the pixel scale right -- resolution is accuracy here.

## How it installs

## Known problems

It is command-line only with no bundled drawing tool, so producing the input is most of the work and the colour convention is easy to get wrong; a mistake there yields a confident number for a structure you did not intend. Convergence is slower the finer the mesh, and a high-resolution bitmap can take a long time. AHRL installs it from apt with no menu entry for the same reason: it is a tool for someone who already knows they need it.
